transcript.note: Round 1 is entirely thinking-order item 3 (shrink the grid), done without giving up a single aligned segment - H/V stays at 98 and the 45 count actually goes up by one. The input is 102x103 but only 34 columns and 46 rows are occupied, so compaction will already strip the empty bands; what compaction cannot do is remove a band that holds exactly one station. I listed every such band and merged the ones whose occupant can reach a neighbouring occupied band along an axis that carries no H/V segment. Rows first: 90/61/35 all slide up into row 22 to join 18, which retires rows 19, 20 and 21 in one go (each is a pure V hanger, so moving the row costs nothing); 71 and 74 into row 33; 51 into row 40; 26 and 73 into row 41; 68 into row 48; 38 into row 53; 64 into row 55; 17, 62 and 41 into row 61, retiring 62 and 64; 85 into row 69; 58 into row 84. Columns: 15 into col 28 (its horizontal to 14 is on row 23 and is untouched), 54 into col 33, 76 into col 82. 50 is the interesting one - it is the only station on col 31 AND the only one on row 54, and it carries a 45 to 52. Rather than break the 45 I moved it diagonally to (33,52), which keeps dx=dy=5 exactly, lands it on the occupied col 33 and retires both bands at once. Deliberately left alone: 30 cannot leave row 60 without breaking its 45 to 29 (its column is pinned by 2 and 41, so row 60 is the only square where |dc|=|dr| holds); 47 and 23 are boxed in by occupied cells on both sides; 1 and 66 would have to break horizontals to move. 9, 77, 95, 42, 57, 59, 72 and 56 sit in bands whose nearest occupied neighbour is 4 or more cells away - they are out of short-move range now, but compaction will pull everything closer and I will revisit them next round.
